findings.title: Java MessageFormat syntax used in an i18next bundle breaks interpolation in the Account Console
findings.body:
The v3 Account Console is a React app that translates with i18next, whose default interpolation is `{{name}}`. The rest of this file follows that convention (e.g. `error-invalid-length='{{0}}' must have ...`).

User-profile server errors are translated client-side: `t(errorMessage, {0: ..., 1: ..., 2: ...})` in `setUserProfileServerError`. With the value changed to `Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.`, i18next performs no substitution. Users would see the literal placeholders and the raw `{2,choice,...}` pattern.

The previous `{{0}}`/`{{1}}`/`{{2}}` form should be kept for the JS bundles. If the verifier needs this key, extend its normalization rather than switching the bundle to MessageFormat syntax.

findings.title: Admin Console bundle switched to MessageFormat placeholders/choice, which i18next cannot render
findings.body:
The admin console (keycloak.v2) also translates with i18next using `{{...}}` interpolation. User-profile validation errors returned by the admin REST API are translated client-side with numeric params.

The new value `Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.` will not be interpolated. Admins creating or editing users with a multivalued-size violation would see raw `{0}` and `{2,choice,...}` text.

The `{{0}}`-style placeholders should be restored for this JS bundle.

findings.title: Lithuanian translation replaced with Italian text
findings.body: `totpStep1` in the Lithuanian bundle is now `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:`, which is Italian. Lithuanian users will see an Italian sentence in the OTP setup page. It should be a Lithuanian phrase, e.g. `Įdiekite vieną iš šių programėlių savo mobiliajame telefone:`.

findings.title: Lithuanian login translation replaced with Italian text
findings.body: `loginTotpStep1` in the Lithuanian login bundle was changed to the Italian `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:`. Lithuanian users configuring OTP at login will see Italian. A Lithuanian translation should be used instead.

findings.title: Simplified Chinese bundle now contains Traditional Chinese text
findings.body: `totpStep1` in `messages_zh_CN` was set to `在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：`. That is Traditional Chinese (手機/安裝/應用程式), apparently copied from zh_TW. The rest of the zh_CN file uses Simplified characters. It should read e.g. `在您的手机上安装以下应用程序之一：`.

findings.title: Diff-trimming logic can throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of reporting the error
findings.body: The `start` and `end` loops that trim common prefix and suffix are computed independently. Neither is bounded by `length - start`, so they can overlap. Example 1: value `y` sanitizes to `y`. That gives start=1 and end=8, and `sanitized.substring(1, 0)` throws. Example 2: value `x` sanitizes to `x`. That gives start=11 and end=4, and `value.substring(11, 7)` throws. The unchecked exception escapes `verify()`, which only catches IOException. The Maven build then fails with a stack trace instead of the intended `Illegal HTML in key ...` message. The end loop should be bounded, e.g. `end < Math.min(value.length(), sanitized.length()) - start`.

findings.title: Anchor mismatch message omits key and file, making failures hard to locate
findings.body:
`santizeAnchors` receives `key` but never uses it. It reports only `Didn't find anchor tag <a ...> in original string`.

When the verifier runs across dozens of message files, a failing build gives no indication of which file or key is at fault. By contrast, the `Illegal HTML` message includes both. The key and `file` should be included in this message.

findings.title: ANCHOR_PATTERN matches any tag starting with 'a', not just anchors
findings.body:
`</?a[^>]*>` also matches `<abbr>`, `<area ...>`, `<audio ...>`, `<article>`, `<aside>`, etc. Any such tag in the English source string is treated as an "anchor" and stripped before sanitization. An identical tag in a translation is therefore accepted without going through the OWASP policy, including any attributes such as event handlers. Non-anchor tags in translations are also misreported as anchor mismatches.

The pattern should be restricted to real anchors, e.g. `</?a(?:\s[^>]*)?>`.
